title: Sugya
description: One Talmudic passage, sentence by sentence, labelled with the move each sentence makes (Derech Tevunos ch. 9) and, optionally, what each sentence is, how it stands to the one it acts on, and what it rests on (ch. 1–8). Everything the page renders and nothing it derives: depth, standing, status, folds and rails are all computed from `units`. Reference: SUGYA_JSON_FORMAT.md at the repository root; implementation: viz/src/format.ts.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editors.

format.description: What kind of file this is.

version.description: Format version. Steps when a key changes meaning or a new one gains a renderer.

title.description: The passage's name in the gallery and the tab: what it is about, in a few words.

folio.description: e.g. "21b-22b". Free text; an editorial remark may follow.

discussedAt.description: Where Ramchal discusses the passage, or the sentence that says he does not and how it was labelled instead.

party.description: Ch. 1: what kind of sugya this is as a whole. Declared, not derived from the speakers.

collection.description: Gallery shelf. `ramchal`: discussed in the book or labelled from its markers. `research`: brought in for the nested-rail study. Absent: shown under its own heading.

about.description: The editor's preface, one paragraph per entry: why the passage is here, how it was labelled, where the taxonomy was stretched. Not printed on the page.

hint.description: Replaces the header's standard copy with where to look on this page. Plain text; `**bold**` and `*italic*` are the only markup.

units.description: The sentences, in the order they are said. A unit's `move.target` must name an earlier unit's `id`.

basis.description: How a label was arrived at: Ramchal's own for this passage; the type's stock word is in the text; ours alone. Absent, it is inferred.

provenance.description: Ch. 8: where the sentence's authority comes from. The first four enter accepted; `derivation` and `asserted` start in doubt. Absent, `asserted`. On a proof, contradiction or difficulty, one of the first four also draws as a ground badge (`ground-sense`, `ground-axiom`, `ground-common-sense`, `ground-tradition`) when the anatomy layer is on and the unit carries no ch. 8 label of its own.

ext.description: Room for what the format does not yet name. Carried through, validated as an object only, read by nothing. When a key here earns a renderer it moves into the schema and `version` steps.

move.description: Ch. 9: what the sentence does. `element/subtype` is the leaf; `target` is the earlier unit it acts on (absent only when it opens: a first statement, a fresh question); `marker` is the stock phrase in the sentence that licensed the label; `attested` says whether Ramchal himself gives the label for this passage.

marker.description: As it appears in the Hebrew, with … for content and פלוני for a name.

annotation.description: One label from a chapter other than 9. Row-level kinds describe the sentence alone; edge-level kinds (relations, deductions, most grounds, `synonymous-terms`, and both ch. 10 composites) describe its move on `target` and need one. `potential` and `actual` are grounds that sit on the row, the two ch. 8 respects (`inseparable-property`, `contingent-attribute`) sit on the row with the statement's anatomy, and the whole of ch. 11 is row-level.

note.description: Why this label: the words in the text that carry it, or the reading.

range.description: A run of words, 1-based and inclusive: "3" is the third word, "2-4" the second to the fourth. Words are the whitespace-separated tokens of the text; punctuation stays with its word. The reader also checks that the range fits the text.

ranges.description: One range, or a list of them where the span is discontinuous in this text (a predicate split around its subject).

span.description: One span: a piece of the sentence playing one role, located in each text the classifier indexed — at least one of `he` / `en`. What is true of the span is written once here, not once per text.

he.description: Where the span is in the Hebrew, as ranges into its words.

en.description: Where the span is in the English, as ranges into its words.

showLoud.description: True only when the passage's logic turns on this span and a reader would miss it. Rare; most passages have none. A loud span is drawn at a trace of its role's hue, a quiet one as a taupe hairline that nearly blends into the paper until 'Detailed spans' is switched on.

note.description: Why these words are this role — not what the role is. A word or two where the span is unimportant (`the rule`, `the carved-out case`), or nothing; a sentence or more where it is loud. A subject or predicate never needs one.

spans.description: Word-level roles: which words of the sentence are its subject and predicate (ch. 3), the antecedent and consequent of a hypothetical (ch. 3), the premises and conclusion of a deduction spelt out in the sentence (ch. 7), and the separate commitments — סוף גזרתו — a challenge can defeat one at a time (ch. 6). By role, each a list of spans in sentence order; each span locates itself in `he` and `en` by ranges into the words, never by copying them.

unit.description: One sentence: its text, who says it, the move it makes, where its authority comes from, its ch. 1–8 and 10–11 labels, and which of its words play which role.

id.description: Unique within the file. Referenced by later units' `move.target`.

speaker.description: Who says it, when the sentence names someone. Absent: the Talmud's own voice.

short.description: A few words naming the sentence, for bands, handles and the minimap. Editorial.

en.description: The sentence in English, as one move.

note.description: Why the label; doubts; where the taxonomy was stretched.
